name: Feedback Prize 2.0 - Classifying Argumentative Elements
task: Multi-class classification of argumentative elements in student writing into 'effective', 'adequate', or 'ineffective' categories.
output_data: A CSV file containing discourse IDs and predicted probabilities for each of the three effectiveness ratings (Ineffective, Adequate, Effective) for each discourse element.
input_data: Student essays in plain text format and corresponding CSV files with annotated discourse elements and their quality ratings.

data file description.sample_submission.csv: A sample submission file demonstrating the required format for predictions, including discourse_id and predicted probabilities for 'Ineffective', 'Adequate', and 'Effective'.
data file description.test: A folder containing example full-text essays from the test set. The actual test set, used for scoring, comprises approximately 3,000 distinct essays.
data file description.test.csv: A CSV file containing annotated discourse elements for the test set essays, including discourse_id, essay_id, discourse_text, discourse_type, and discourse_type_num, but without the target 'discourse_effectiveness' column.
data file description.train: A folder containing full-text essays in .txt format, where each file name corresponds to an essay_id found in train.csv.
data file description.train.csv: A CSV file containing annotated discourse elements for the training set essays. It includes discourse_id, essay_id, discourse_text, discourse_type, discourse_type_num, and the target quality rating 'discourse_effectiveness' (Ineffective, Adequate, Effective).
data file description.*.txt: Individual plain text files representing full student essays, identified by their essay_id (e.g., 0029f4d19c3f.txt). These files are located in the 'train/' and 'test/' folders.

task: Build multilingual machine learning models to identify toxicity in online conversations, specifically predicting the probability that a comment is toxic, using English-only training data and non-English test data.
input_data: The input data consists of comment text. Training data (jigsaw-toxic-comment-train.csv and jigsaw-unintended-bias-train.csv) contains English comments from Wikipedia talk pages and Civil Comments, along with a 'toxic' label (0 or 1). Test data (test.csv) contains comments from Wikipedia talk pages in various non-English languages, without the 'toxic' label.

data file description.jigsaw-toxic-comment-train.csv: Training data from the first Jigsaw competition, consisting of English comments from Wikipedia’s talk page edits with toxicity labels.
data file description.jigsaw-unintended-bias-train.csv: Training data from the second Jigsaw competition, an expanded version of the Civil Comments dataset with additional labels.
data file description.sample_submission.csv: A sample submission file demonstrating the correct format for predictions.
data file description.test.csv: Comments from Wikipedia talk pages in different non-English languages, used for testing the multilingual models.

output_data: A CSV file with two columns: 'id' (identifier from the test set) and 'toxic' (the predicted probability that the comment is toxic).
name: Jigsaw Multilingual Toxic Comment Classification

data file description.submission_file01.csv: Sample submission file with the correct format.
data file description.test.csv: Data to predict, contains: ID, Title.
data file description.train.csv: Data to train the model, contains: ID, Title, Domain.

name: H2O.ai Hackathon - LLM Model Detection

data file description.sample_submission.csv: Illustrates the required submission format, consisting of columns 'id' and 'target_0' through 'target_6' (probabilities for each of the 7 models).
data file description.test.csv: Contains 'id', 'Question', and 'Response' columns. Participants must predict the likely LLM model for each response.
data file description.train.csv: Contains 'Question', 'Response', and 'target' (with values 0-6) columns, used for training machine learning models.

output_data: A CSV file with 'id' and probability columns (target_0 to target_6) for each of the 7 possible models.
task: Multi-class classification to detect which of 7 possible LLM models produced a given text output.

input_data: Tabular data (pet profiles), free-text descriptions, pet images, and supplementary data derived from Google Vision API (image metadata) and Google Natural Language API (sentiment analysis of descriptions). Auxiliary lookup tables for breeds, colors, and states are also provided.

data file description.train.csv: Tabular and text data for the training set, containing pet profiles and their actual adoption speeds.
data file description.test.csv: Tabular and text data for the test set, containing pet profiles for which adoption speeds need to be predicted.
data file description.sample_submission.csv: A sample submission file demonstrating the correct format for predictions.
data file description.breed_labels.csv: Lookup table containing breed IDs, types (dog/cat), and breed names.
data file description.color_labels.csv: Lookup table containing color IDs and color names.
data file description.state_labels.csv: Lookup table containing state IDs and state names in Malaysia.
data file description.train_images: Folder containing image files for pets in the training set. Images are named 'PetID-ImageNumber.jpg'.
data file description.test_images: Folder containing image files for pets in the test set. Images are named 'PetID-ImageNumber.jpg'.
data file description.train_metadata: Folder containing JSON files with Google Vision API analysis (Face Annotation, Label Annotation, Text Annotation, Image Properties) for images in the training set. Files are named 'PetID-ImageNumber.json'.
data file description.test_metadata: Folder containing JSON files with Google Vision API analysis (Face Annotation, Label Annotation, Text Annotation, Image Properties) for images in the test set. Files are named 'PetID-ImageNumber.json'.
data file description.train_sentiment: Folder containing JSON files with Google Natural Language API analysis (sentiment and key entities) for pet descriptions in the training set. Files are named 'PetID.json'.
data file description.test_sentiment: Folder containing JSON files with Google Natural Language API analysis (sentiment and key entities) for pet descriptions in the test set. Files are named 'PetID.json'.

output_data: A CSV file named 'submission.csv' with two columns: 'PetID' and 'AdoptionSpeed' (predicted adoption speed).
task: Predicting the adoptability of pets, specifically how quickly a pet is adopted, based on their online profiles. This is a multi-class classification task with 5 possible outcomes (0-4) for adoption speed.
name: Petfinder Adoption Prediction

input_data: Images (JPG files) and associated textual captions and labels (from train.csv and test.csv).
output_data: Predicted labels for test set images, submitted as a CSV file.

data file description.train.csv: The training dataset, containing ImageID, Labels (1-19, 12 missing), and Caption.
data file description.test.csv: The test dataset, containing ImageID and Caption for which labels need to be predicted.
data file description.data: Folder containing all image files (JPG format) referenced by ImageID in train.csv and test.csv.

name: University of Sydney, School of Computer Science, COMP5329, 2025 Semester1, Assignment2, Competition Track

output_data: The output should be a CSV file with a header, containing the unique ID for each image in the test set, followed by predicted probabilities for each of the 120 dog breeds. The submission is evaluated on Multi Class Log Loss.

data file description.custom_competition_data: The root directory containing the competition datasets.
data file description.labels.csv: A CSV file containing the unique IDs and corresponding breed labels for the images in the training set.
data file description.sample_submission.csv: A sample submission file demonstrating the correct format, including image IDs and placeholder probabilities for each breed.
data file description.test: A folder containing images for the test set. For these images, breed probabilities must be predicted.
data file description.train: A folder containing images for the training set, for which breed labels are provided in 'labels.csv'.
data file description.*.jpg: Individual image files of dogs, named by their unique ID, located within the 'train' and 'test' folders.

name: Dog Breed Identification
task: Fine-grained image classification to identify the breed of a dog from its photo.
input_data: The input data consists of a training set and a test set of dog images. Each image is identified by a unique ID. The dataset covers 120 distinct dog breeds. The training set images have corresponding breed labels provided in 'labels.csv'.
A training dataset of 10,407 labeled paddy leaf images with metadata (variety, age) and an unlabeled test dataset of 3,469 paddy leaf images.

data file description.train.csv: The training set metadata, including unique image identifiers (image_id), the target disease label, paddy variety, and age of the paddy in days.
data file description.sample_submission.csv: A sample submission file demonstrating the required format for predictions, with image_id and label columns.
data file description.train_images: A directory containing 10,407 training paddy leaf images. Filenames correspond to the image_id column in train.csv.
data file description.test_images: A directory containing 3,469 test paddy leaf images for which disease predictions are to be made.
data file description.test.csv: Metadata for the test set, likely containing image_id for the test images.

name: Paddy Disease Classification
output_data: A CSV file containing image IDs and their predicted paddy disease labels (one of ten categories, including normal leaf).

The output is a submission file in CSV format, containing 'id' and the predicted probabilities for each of the 7 defect categories: Pastry, Z_Scratch, K_Scatch, Stains, Dirtiness, Bumps, Other_Faults.
name: Kaggle Playground Series - Steel Plates Faults
input_data: The input data consists of 'train.csv' for training models, which includes features and 7 binary target variables, and 'test.csv' for making predictions, which contains only features. The dataset is synthetically generated from the Steel Plates Faults dataset from UCI.
task: Predict the probability of various defects on steel plates (multi-label binary classification).

data file description.sample_submission.csv: A sample submission file in the correct format, showing the expected structure for predictions.
data file description.test.csv: The test dataset containing features for which predictions of the 7 binary targets are required.
data file description.train.csv: The training dataset, which includes features and the 7 binary target variables: Pastry, Z_Scratch, K_Scatch, Stains, Dirtiness, Bumps, Other_Faults.

data file description.train_images: Folder containing JPEG images for training.
data file description.train.csv: CSV file with labels (target traits) and ancillary data (satellite, soil, climate) for each training image.
data file description.test_images: Folder containing JPEG images for testing, used to create predictions for submission.
data file description.test.csv: CSV file with ancillary data (satellite, soil, climate) for each test image.
data file description.target_name_meta.tsv: TSV file providing full names of the plant traits obtained from the TRY database.
data file description.sample_submission.csv: An example CSV file demonstrating the correct format for submission.

output_data: A CSV file containing predictions for 6 plant traits (e.g., X1080, X50) for each image, identified by a unique 'id'.
task: Predict 6 plant traits (e.g., leaf area, plant height) from crowd-sourced plant images and ancillary geodata using deep learning regression models.
name: PlantTraits2024 Challenge
input_data: Crowd-sourced plant images (JPEG) and associated ancillary geodata including climate variables (WORLDCLIM), soil properties (SOIL), and multitemporal satellite data (MODIS, VOD). For training, species-specific trait standard deviations are also provided.
